findings.excerpt:
theorem LieIdeal.topEquiv_apply (x : (⊤ : LieIdeal R L)) : LieIdeal.topEquiv x = x :=
  rfl
findings.problem: `LieIdeal.topEquiv` is a new `def`, so simp does not unfold it. Its application lemma `topEquiv_apply` is the only simp-level handle on it, and it carries no `@[simp]`. The analogous `LieSubalgebra.topEquiv_apply` in `Submodule.lean` is tagged `@[simp]`, so the two top-equivalences are inconsistent. A goal containing `LieIdeal.topEquiv x` stays stuck under `simp`.
findings.proposed_change: Mark the lemma `@[simp]`, as in `LieSubalgebra.topEquiv_apply`: `@[simp] theorem LieIdeal.topEquiv_apply ...`.
findings.benefit: Simp can then rewrite `LieIdeal.topEquiv x` to the coercion `↑x`. This is the canonical form, and it matches the behaviour of the subalgebra version, so users do not need to unfold the definition by hand.

findings.excerpt: theorem map_toSubmodule (h : ↑(map f I) = f '' I) :
findings.problem: The `@[simp]` lemma has the hypothesis `h : ↑(map f I) = f '' I`. This is a nontrivial set equation, and it is exactly the fact that makes `map` agree with the plain image. Simp can only use the lemma if it can prove that equation, and no simp lemma in the file does so for a general `f`. The attribute is therefore very unlikely to fire. In the file, the only use is the explicit `I.map_toSubmodule f h` in `comap_map_eq`. The unconditional general-case fact (the surjective case) is `coe_map_of_surjective`, which is not simp.
findings.proposed_change: Remove `@[simp]` from `map_toSubmodule`. If a simp normal form for `toSubmodule (map f I)` is wanted, tag a lemma whose hypothesis simp can discharge, for example `coe_map_of_surjective` with `Function.Surjective f`, which is the usual form of such side conditions. Otherwise leave it as an explicit rewrite lemma.
findings.benefit: The simp set no longer contains a lemma that is almost never applicable. The remaining simp interface is more honest, and simp lemmas that really apply are not obscured.

findings.excerpt: theorem comap_map_eq (h : ↑(map f I) = f '' I) : comap f (map f I) = I ⊔ f.ker := by
findings.problem: This `@[simp]` lemma has the same kind of side condition: the equation `↑(map f I) = f '' I`. Simp cannot discharge it for a generic `f` and `I`. The lemma also has a right-hand side `I ⊔ f.ker` that adds a join, so it would only be a normal form when the hypothesis is available. For `comap f (map f I)`, the lemma therefore fires either almost never or only when a matching hypothesis is in context. A fully unconditional fact, `comap_map_le`, is present but not simp, so the file does not offer a reliable normal form.
findings.proposed_change: Remove `@[simp]` from `comap_map_eq`. Alternatively, add a separate simp lemma for the surjective case, where the side condition is the discharged-by-assumption `Function.Surjective f`, and derive it using `coe_map_of_surjective`.
findings.benefit: This avoids a simp lemma that suggests coverage it does not provide. If the surjective variant is added, simp users get a lemma that actually applies, since a surjectivity hypothesis is easy to supply to simp.
